question.problem: Consider the curve $r(t)=⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,2-3\operatorname{cos}⁡4t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=12t.$ Find $R(s),$ the parametrization of the curve by its arc length $s.$

current_example.problem: Consider the curve  $\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle 2t-1 ,\: 8t+2 ,\: -2t \right\rangle, \, t \geq 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $\mathbf{r}(0)$ to $\mathbf{r}(t)$ is given by $s=6\sqrt{2}t.$ Find $\mathbf R(s),$ the parametrization of the curve by its arc length $s.$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, since  $s=6\sqrt{2}t,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}6\sqrt{2}t & =s \\ t & =\frac{s}{6\sqrt{2}} \\ t & =\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

The vector function that pametrizes the curve $\mathbf r(t)$ by its arc length $s,$ with $s \geq 0,$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12}) \\  & =⟨2(\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12})-1,\,8(\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12})+2,\,-2(\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{6}-1,\,\frac{4\sqrt{2}s}{6}+2,\,-\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{6}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨\sqrt{2}s-6,\,4\sqrt{2}s+12,\,-\sqrt{2}s⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
